action_items.task: Check project requirements to confirm if the device should be used only for television or also for DVD/internet, and update the team.

decisions.text: Teletext and speech recognition features are removed from the remote.
The remote will use a separate radio sender for the location finder, sold as a two-part package.
The location finder will use a buzzer output instead of a light.
The remote will focus on DVD and TV control, dropping VCR capabilities.
The remote will include a red power button and number keys.

notes:
## Usability Test Results
- Users dislike the look, feel, and mismatch with operating behavior of current remotes.
- Users only use 10% of available buttons; most used are for channel selection (160 times/hour), teletext, volume, and power.
- Settings buttons are rarely used (less than 0.8 times/hour).
## Target Audience and Pricing
- Users aged 15-35 are willing to pay more for the product (91% to 76%).
- Users over 35 are less willing to pay, dropping to 8% for those over 65.
## Design and Functionality
- The remote will have basic functions for channel and volume control, plus a location finder feature.
- Speech recognition was discussed but rejected due to programming difficulty and budget constraints.
- Teletext is considered outdated and has been removed from the scope.
- The remote will focus on TV control only, excluding internet features.
## Hardware and Location Finder
- The location finder will use a radio signal sent from a separate sender attached to the TV or wall, rather than IR.
- The sender will be sold separately from the remote.
- The location finder will use a buzzer output instead of a light.
## Circular Touch Control Interface
- The interface is a flat touch disc using the same technology as a mouse pad.
- Users can scroll their thumb around the circle to navigate channels or tracks.
- A specific region of the circle can be pressed to 'zap' or perform specific actions.
- The iPod's wheel is re-programmable and can be used for volume control by pressing a middle region.
## Device Compatibility and Functionality
- The device needs to be compatible with channel selection for TV.
- DVD players typically have their own remotes, but consolidating controls is desirable.
- Volume is usually controlled on the TV, so the remote might not need dedicated volume buttons for DVD.
- A function switch button may be needed to toggle between TV, DVD, and VCR modes.
## Next Steps
- Attendees will finish questionnaires and work individually after lunch.
- Bring new ideas to the next meeting.
tldr: The team finalized the design of a new remote control focusing on a circular touch interface for TV and DVD, removed speech recognition and teletext features, and defined the target audience as teenagers and young professionals.
